footerTagline: A volunteer-led community cinema, travelling through film.

home.heroStandfirst: We bring films from around the world to different places, and bring people together around them. Each screening is a chance to share a story, meet new people, and see somewhere familiar or far away.
home.manifestoLede: Cinema can help us travel, not only to different places but towards one another.
manifestoBody: Passenger Cinema was founded in London in 2024 on a simple idea: that a film can put you somewhere you have never been, next to someone you would never otherwise have met.

Every event starts with the same question: where should this film live? We have screened in an independent cinema, a film school, a 1920s picture palace, a basement in Dalston and a craft café, choosing the room that suits the story. Each new space introduces Passenger Cinema to a different local community.
No two Passenger Cinema events are the same. That keeps us creatively challenged, and it keeps our audience curious about where we’ll take them next.

pillars.label: 01 / Travel
pillars.title: Travelling the world through films
pillars.body: Films transport us to different places and immerse us in new cultures without leaving our seats. With each screening we bring that sense of exploration and cultural discovery, one country at a time.

pillars.label: 02 / Community
pillars.title: A hub, not an audience
pillars.body: People from very different backgrounds connect over the universal language of cinema. Our events are a space to meet, exchange stories and build connections that outlast the credits.

pillars.label: 03 / Culture
pillars.title: Celebration, not tourism
pillars.body: We welcome people who are part of the culture on screen alongside those discovering it for the first time. That mix is the whole point: it’s how a screening becomes empathy rather than spectacle.

home.involvedHeading: Passenger Cinema is made by the people who turn up.
home.involvedRecommend: Our programme comes from our audience as much as from us. Tell us about a film you think London should see, or a room you think would make a beautiful cinema for a day.
home.involvedVolunteer: We are entirely volunteer-led. Programmers, photographers, writers, illustrators, front-of-house, people who are good at carrying things: we want all of you, and we want your own creative work in our events too.

screenings.heading: What’s on
screenings.standfirst: We programme one journey at a time, and we build the whole event around it: the room, the food, the music, the people who know the film best.
screenings.firstTimeHeading: What actually happens at a Passenger Cinema event?

firstTime.label: Before
firstTime.title: Come on your own
firstTime.body: Plenty of people do. Doors open early on purpose so there is time to get a drink and talk to someone before the lights go down.

firstTime.label: During
firstTime.title: A short introduction, then the film
firstTime.body: We say a few words about why we chose it and who helped us bring it here. Then we get out of the way.

firstTime.label: After
firstTime.title: The part people remember
firstTime.body: A workshop, a meal, a live set, a Q&A, a conversation that runs long. This is the half of the event that turns an audience into a room of people who know each other.

archive.heading: Where we’ve been
archive.standfirst: Every screening we have ever put on, in reverse order. Each one had a different room, a different set of collaborators and a different reason for existing.

recommend.heading: Where should we go next?
recommend.standfirst: Some of our best events have started with someone telling us about a film we’d never heard of, or offering a room nobody had thought of using as a cinema. Both are below.
filmIntro: It doesn’t need to be obscure and it doesn’t need to be worthy. It needs to be worth building an event around. Tell us why it matters to you.
If it’s a film from a culture you belong to, say so, because we would love to make it with you rather than about you.
venueIntro: We have screened in a basement music venue, a members’ bar, a 1920s picture palace, a 16mm film club, a film school, a bookshop cinema and a craft café on its opening weekend.
You don’t need a projector, a screen or blackout blinds. We have brought all three before, along with a bedsheet and a lot of volunteers.

volunteer.heading: Create journeys with us
volunteer.standfirst: Passenger Cinema is a volunteer-led community, and we want everyone who contributes to feel that they are genuinely part of what we are building.
volunteer.offerIntro: We hope Passenger Cinema can be a space where you can experiment, meet like-minded people and become part of a growing community built around cinema, culture and storytelling.
offer: Shape Passenger Cinema with us. Contribute to our projects, screenings and events, and have a real voice in how the community develops.
Hands-on experience working inside an independent cultural organisation, involved in the creative process behind our events.
Meet and collaborate with filmmakers, artists and creatives working across cinema, culture and the arts.
Attend our screenings and events as part of the team.
Monthly team meetings, online or in person where we can, so you always know what is coming up and have a say in shaping it.
Build your portfolio. Use the work you make with Passenger Cinema in your own professional or creative practice.

Space for your own creative work. If you’re an artist or filmmaker, we want Passenger Cinema to be a platform for your creativity too: your illustrations or artwork in our posters and visual materials, your short films screened at our events, or another way of bringing your work into the room.
An annual membership to The Prince Charles Cinema, so you have another space to keep watching and discovering all year.

about.heading: We go wherever the film belongs.
about.standfirst: Passenger Cinema was founded in London in 2024 on a simple idea: cinema can help us travel, not only to different places but towards one another.
body: Every screening is an invitation to discover a new country, meet new people and experience a culture through film.

Our programme reflects the diversity of the city we call home. Every event brings together people of different ages, nationalities and backgrounds around a shared experience, proving that cinema can create common ground even when we don’t share the same language or story.

We have travelled through cinema to Turkey, Japan, Brazil, Mexico, Jamaica, Italy, Hong Kong, Spain and Iran, celebrating stories that are rarely given the spotlight in mainstream cinemas. We believe audiences are curious and adventurous, and our programming reflects that. We have been proud to welcome people from the cultures represented on screen alongside those discovering them for the first time, creating conversations that continue long after the credits roll.
about.teamNote: Beyond the two of us, Passenger Cinema is a rotating crew of volunteers: programmers, photographers, designers, writers, front-of-house, and friends who turn up with projectors, sound systems and, on one occasion, weaving looms carried over from Turkey.

support.heading: Help us keep travelling.
support.standfirst: Passenger Cinema is run entirely by volunteers. Nobody takes a wage. What we raise goes straight back into the next screening.
body: Every event has to pay for itself before it can happen. A licence for the film, a room for the day, a projector and a sound system if the room hasn't got them, and the posters that get people through the door.

Ticket prices cover most of it, and we keep them deliberately low so that money is never the reason someone doesn't come. Donations are what close the gap, and what let us take a risk on a film nobody has heard of.
uses: Film licences. The single biggest cost, and the one nobody sees. A licence runs from around £100 to £250 per screening.
Rooms. Some spaces host us for nothing. Most do not.
Kit. Projectors, screens and sound for the rooms that have none.
Keeping tickets low, so that cost is never the reason someone stays home.
Taking a risk on a film with no audience yet, which is usually the one worth showing.
support.sponsorLede: If you are a company, a venue or a funder, there is more we could do together.
support.sponsorBody: We have partnered with cinemas, film schools, craft spaces, restaurants and cultural organisations across London, Istanbul, Barcelona and Dublin. Sponsorship can mean funding a screening, hosting one, or bringing something to it that we could not make ourselves.

subscribe.heading: Never miss a screening.
subscribe.body: Leave your email and we will tell you when the next one is announced. No newsletter, no digest, nothing else: just the events.

award.heading: Emerging Community Cinema of the Year.
award.body: In 2025 we won the Emerging Community Cinema Award at the Film Society of the Year Awards, run by Cinema For All and sponsored by WRS Insurance. It came in the year community cinema in Britain turned a hundred, which made it feel like being handed a place in a much longer story.
